article.title: Why ‘Same Sales’ Can Hide Very Different Customer Behavior
article.why: Learn why total sales alone cannot explain how customers are behaving.

paragraphs.en:
Two stores can report the same sales and still have very different customer behavior. Imagine Store A and Store B each make one million yen this month. At first, their performance looks identical. But the total does not tell us how the sales were created.

Store A may have 100 customers who each spend 10,000 yen. Store B may have 200 customers who each spend 5,000 yen. The sales total is the same, but the customer structure is different. Store A depends on fewer, higher-spending customers. Store B serves more customers with a smaller average spend.

Frequency creates another difference. One customer may visit once and spend 10,000 yen. Another may visit five times and spend 2,000 yen each time. Their monthly spending is equal, but their relationship with the store is not. Frequent visits may create more opportunities for future purchases, while a single large purchase may be connected to a special event.

This is why analysts often break sales into several parts: number of customers, visits per customer, and spending per visit. If total sales rise, this decomposition helps explain whether growth came from more customers, more frequent visits, or larger baskets.

The same idea matters when sales stay flat. A stable total can hide a warning sign. For example, customer count may fall while spending per remaining customer rises. The business still reports the same sales today, but it may be becoming dependent on a smaller group. The opposite can also happen: many new customers arrive, but each spends less.

A useful report therefore does not stop at ‘sales were unchanged.’ It asks what changed underneath the total. Looking at customer count, frequency, and basket size gives managers a clearer picture of whether customer behavior is becoming stronger, weaker, or simply different.
paragraphs.zh:
兩家店即使總銷售額相同，顧客行為也可能完全不同。A店可能100位顧客各花1萬日圓，B店則200位顧客各花5,000日圓；總額一樣，但顧客結構不同。來店頻率也會造成差異：一次花1萬與五次各花2,000，月消費相同，與店家的關係卻不同。

因此分析 sales 時，常拆成 customer count、visits per customer 與 spending per visit。即使總額不變，也可能藏著顧客數下降、剩餘顧客客單上升等風險。好的報告不應停在「sales unchanged」，而要解釋總額底下究竟是哪個行為因子改變。
paragraphs.ja:
同じ売上でも顧客行動は同じとは限りません。100人が1万円ずつ使う店と、200人が5千円ずつ使う店では売上は同じでも顧客構成が違います。来店頻度も重要で、1回1万円と5回2千円では月間利用額は同じでも関係性は異なります。

そのためsalesはcustomer count、visits per customer、spending per visitに分解して考えます。売上が横ばいでも、顧客数減少を残存顧客の高単価が補っている可能性があります。「売上は変わらない」で終わらず、その下の行動変化を見ることが重要です。
